column1: # Where each woven Latin plural in lex-la.tsv was read.
# A noun row weaves its second form under an English plural, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. Its sound has been held to
# Allen & Greenough since 2026-10-04, and its spelling to nothing: Lewis &
# Short prints a noun's genitive and gender, not its plural. English
# Wiktionary declines every Latin noun in a table whose cells carry a class
# per slot, and on 2026-10-08 every woven plural was read in the rendered
# table (action=render) of its entry: the cell classed nom|p, quoted as the
# table prints it with every form the cell holds, "nominative plural locī".
# tests/tools/la-forms.test.ts fails on a plural changed in one file and not
# the other, a line citing another word's entry, a quote from another cell or
# not printing its plural, and a line outliving its row.
# One entry per line, the one whose table the quote is from:
# A noun's is its headword's. Wiktionary files a verb under its first
# person, the key Lewis & Short files it under in la-glosses.tsv, so a verb's
# is that key's, j written i and the homograph number dropped: dīcere is
# A page holding more than one word of a spelling is read by the table whose
# headword is this one, Wiktionary marking each table's with its vowel
# lengths: ōs, the mouth, "ōra", beside os, the bone, "ossa, ossua"; liber,
# All 165 are among the forms their table prints. aliēnus, woven for
# "stranger", is an adjective used as a noun, Lewis & Short's "Subst.", and
# its page declines it as one: its line quotes the cell of its gender,
# classed nom|m|p, "masculine nominative plural aliēnī", the form woven, and
# ADJECTIVE in tests/tools/la-forms.test.ts names it for the test to read
